## Interesting questions, provocative answers

Why do petrostates attempt to reconstitute their image as leaders in
the energy transition? 

- who or what is driving the change (or lack thereof) and for whom is the narrative constructed? 
- How does the state define transition? 

> "the principal audience for this narrative is a domestic, regional, and primarily Arabic-speaking one."

## Contribution 

There are always competing frames, even without competing media.

Domestic politics of IR (Aklin and Mildenberger, 2020; Colgan and Hale, 2021; Colgan and Genovese, 2025; Green, 2025)

- Are the "political frames" domestic? Disaggregation?

## Next steps 

Co-occurrence of frames with 

- How bad?
- Who decides? 
- What to do? 
    - mitigation (taxes, subsidies)
    - adaptation/resilience (green, grey, behavioral)
    - compensation (types of loss and damage)
    - relocation/migration (aid, restrict)
    
This will add richness & clarify what paradigms imply. 

## Next steps 

Co-occurrence of frames with other frames

- Cashore and Bernstein (2023) "commons (Type 1), economic optimization (Type 2), compromise (Type 3), and prioritization (Type 4)" 
- "Deep green"
- etc.

This will add richness & clarify what frames imply.

It will also help you speak to more scholarly and practitioner communities.
